***48 HOUR PHMSA UPDATE FOR REPORT 1198866*** ORIGINAL REPORT: **UPDATE TO A PREVIOUS NRC REPORT** THE RP IS REPORTING A RELEASE OF NATURAL GAS DUE TO A THIRD PARTY STRIKING AN UNDERGROUND PIPELINE. THE INCIDENT INVOLVES A FARMING TILING MACHINE. RP REPORTS THERE WAS AN IGNITION DUE TO THE STRIKE AND THE LOCAL FD REPORTS THAT THERE WERE TWO (2) INJURIES AND TWO (2) REPORTED FATALITIES. RP STATED THE TWO INJURED INDIVIDUALS WERE TRANSPORTED TO A LOCAL HOSPITAL. RP STATED THAT THE LOCAL FIRE CHIEF CONFIRMED THE TWO FATALITIES. NO REPORTED EVACUATIONS. THE AREA WAS SECURED AND ROADS WERE CLOSED. THE AMOUNT RELEASED IS BELIEVED TO EXCEED THE 3000 MCF. DAMAGE COST ARE CURRENTLY UNKNOWN. **THE LINE IS CLASS 1, DOT REGULATED. 20" DIAMETER, .281 WALL THICKNESS. X40 GRADE. **MAOP IS 800. OPERATING PRESSURE AT THE TIME OF THE INCIDENT WAS IN THE LOW 700S. 13.6 MILES OF PIPE WAS ISOLATED IN RESPONSE TO THE INCIDENT. **ORIGINAL NRC# 1198853** CALLER REPORTS A RELEASE OF AN UNKNOWN AMOUNT OF NATURAL GAS INTO AIR CAUSED BY AN UNKNOWN REASON FROM A PIPELINE. ***UPDATED INFORMATION: UPDATES TO RELEASE VOLUME AND REPAIR COST.

DUE TO EXTENSIVE PROPERTY DAMAGE AND NUMEROUS INJURIES IN THE IMMEDIATE AREA AS A RESULT OF THE TORNADO, PLANT HAZMAT AND REFRIGERATION CREWS WERE DELAYED IN RESPONDING TO THE SITUATION. PLANT HAZMAT CREWS WERE ONSITE AND ABLE TO MAKE AN ASSESSMENT OF THE AMMONIA SYSTEM INTEGRITY AT APPROXIMATELY 21:30 CDT.

REPORT DATE: 08-22-2026 REPORT TIME: 2014 UTC REGION: GULF OF AMERICA SUB REGION: N/A AREA/BLOCK: WEST CAMERON 658 IMAGE DATE: 08-22-2026 IMAGE TIME: 1645 UTC DATA SOURCE: LANDSAT9 MODE: MULTISPECTRAL RESOLUTION: 30 METER LOCATION: 27°52'14" N/93°15'39" W AREA: 1.02 SQUARE KILOMETERS CONFIDENCE: MEDIUM REPORT MAP/GIS FILES: HTTPS://WWW.OSPO.NOAA.GOV/PRODUCTS/OCEAN/MARINEPOLLUTION/ REMARKS: POSSIBLE OIL WAS OBSERVED IN SATELLITE IMAGERY. THIS ANOMALY IS UNCONFIRMED AS OIL. IT WAS LOCATED IN THE WEST CAMERON LEASE AREA OF THE GULF. THE ANOMALY MEASURED APPROXIMATELY 4.53 NM IN LENGTH AND WAS 0.11 NM AT ITS WIDEST. THE LINEAR SLICK LOOKED DARK AGAINST THE WATER AND EXHIBITED SHARP EDGES. THE ANOMALY WAS LIKELY RELATED TO PREVIOUS NOAA NESDIS RESPONSELINK REPORTS INCLUDING #1471298 FROM 8/20, #1470887 FROM 8/16, #1470872 FROM 8/15, #1470568 FROM 8/12, #1470355 FROM 8/10, #1470134 FROM 8/8, AND #1470016 FROM 8/6. THERE IS AN ANTI-FREEZE DRUM LEAKING WHEN IT IS USED, BUT THE PREFERENCE SEEMS TO BE DUMPING THE ANTI-FREEZE DOWN THE UTILITY SINK DRAIN, WHICH HAS BEEN WITNESSED BY THE ORIGINAL REPORTING PARTY.
